newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
KULMAR TOP "OWNER/DRIVER" AT MUMM 36 WORLDS
Australian yachtsmen STEVE KULMAR and RICHARD FRIEDRICHS should be pleased with their performance at the Mumm 36 World championships which ended last weekend.

The hotly-contested, 11-race series in the Mediterranean, sailed from Punta Ala on the Tuscany coast of Italy, attracted many of the best professional sailors in the world as helmsmen, tacticians and sail trimmers.
KULMAR and his crew of largely amateur sailors from Sydney's Royal Prince Alfred yacht Club were right up among the leaders in many races in their new Mumm 36, Sea.

Their results included a third, a fourth and two sixths in the 21-boat fleet. While they finished 10th overall, they were less than 10 points out of sixth place in a star-studded fleet which saw the lead change almost daily.

KULMAR, a Sydney advertising executive, won the "owner/driver" award, showing his helming skills against such renowned international helmsmen as New Zealanders GAVIN BRADY, DAVID BARNES and TOM DODSON, American CHRIS LARSEN, Brazil's Olympic gold medallist TORBEN GRAEL and Italy's TOMMASO CHIEFFI.
Overall winner was the German yacht Thomas I Punkt, owned by THOMAS FRIESE but helmed by Kiwi GAVIN BRADY.

Ireland's Jameson, steered by American CHRIS LARSON for TOM ROCHE, was second. Italy's Breeze placed third while the New Zealand Admiral's Cup boat, Georgia Express, steered by TOM DODSON for owner JIM FARMER finished an impressive fourth.

Thomas I Punkt's victory gave her a place in Germany's team for the Admiral's Cup. Six of the top 10 placings in the Mumm 36 Worlds will represent their countries in six weeks in the Champagne Mumm Admiral's Cup at Cowes, England.

KULMAR and FRIEDRICHS, a Sydney marketing and promotions executive, and the crew of Sea will be joined at Cowes by team captain SYD FISCHER with his new Farr 49, Ragamuffin, and the ILC 40, G Net, which has been chartered by Melbourne stockbroker JOHN CALVERT-JONES and Sydney marina owner ROBIN CRAWFORD.
AUSTRALIANS RANK WELL IN OLYMPIC CLASSES

As Australia's Olympic sailors head for Europe (some are already there) to begin their international campaigns leading towards Sydney 2000, the International Sailing Federation's latest O'Neill world sailing rankings are most encouraging.
The rankings show Australians are ranked high up in seven of the ten Olympic classes.

In the Tornado catamaran class, Barcelona and Atlanta medallist MITCH BOOTH and his new crew, ADAM BEASHEL, are ranked a close fourth after their win at the Spa Regatta in the Netherlands, behind German, Spanish and Austrian crews.
They have a heavy campaign ahead of them next month, starting with the European championships and the famous Kieler Woche Regatta in Germany.
MATT HAYES, STEVE JARVIN and STEPHEN McCONAGHY, who represented Australia in the Soling class in the Olympic sailing regatta at Savannah, are ranked fourth.
They will be heading for Denmark and the Soling World championships, along with six other Australian crews.
The 49er high performance dinghy, the newest Olympic class, has been included in the rankings for the first time with regattas in Australia, Europe and the U.S. counting.
No 49er crew has yet competed in more than three ranked events, so all points scored count.
Australia's WARWICK ROOKLYN and TIM WEBSTER head the rankings, just ahead of Americans JONATHAN and CHARLIE McKEE, MORGAN LARSON and TIM BAYLIS.

Two other Australian crews are in the top 15 -- PETER WARNER and TIM HALES and DAVID LUMB and MATT LEVY -- but Sail Sydney '97 winner CHRIS NICHOLSON has not sailed enough regattas to be listed in the rankings.

Other Australian Sailing Squad members in the top Olympic class rankings are Mistral sailboarders BRENDAN TODD (11) and NATASHA STURGES (6), Laser sailor MICHAEL BLACKBURN (8) and JENNIFER LIDGETT and ADDY BUCEK, who rank sixth in the 470 women's class.
ADDY is expected to sail with a new skipper in the 470s.
GONG FOR SAILING ADMIRAL
Didn't notice many yachties among the Queen's Birthday Honours but one regular offshore sailor to be recognised for his role in the Royal Australian Navy was Rear Admiral PETER BRIGGS AM, CSC, RAN.
Admiral BRIGGS was awarded an AO (Military Division) for distinguished service to the RAN in his position as Flag Officer commanding Navy Training Command.
A keen sailor, he has been a regular competitor in the Ocean Racing Club of Victoria's offshore races over the past couple of seasons as navigator aboard the Navy's Melbourne-based yachts.
EXILE FOR NOUMEA RACE

This year's revival of the Australia-New Caledonia ocean race has been given a boost with Sydney-based Guess watches maker WARWICK MILLER entering his mean, green machine Exile for September's race across the southwest Pacific to Noumea.

MILLER plans to sail the 66-foot pocket maxi in the TAG Heuer-Ansett Australia Hayman Island Big Boat Series and the XXXX-Ansett Hamilton Island Race Week in the Whitsundays in August and then bring her back for the Brisbane-to-Noumea race.

The Brisbane-Noumea race is being conducted by Queensland's Cruising Yacht Club while the Sydney-Noumea leg has been taken over by the Royal Prince Alfred Yacht Club. The host club is again the hospitable Cercle Nautique Caledonien.

Meanwhile, the Hayman Island Big Boat Series organisers have announced that the Joico Trophy, a spectacular crystal bowl, will become a centrepiece among the fine array of awards at this year's event at the prestigious holiday resort.

ANTON STARLING, the Sydney-based chairman of the Sabre Corporation who contested the inaugural Big Boat Series in his maxi yacht Fudge (ex Matador), has given the trophy for the champion yacht in the invitation-only fleet of 20 boats.

In addition to Exile, owners who have accepted invitations to compete in the August 17-21 regatta include GEORGE SNOW with his revamped Brindabella, PETER WALKER with Foxtel Amazon and CHARLES CURRAN with Sydney.
RECORD ENTRY FOR SWAN REGATTA

One of the most prestigious events in Europe next month will be the Rolex Swan European Regatta, with the exclusive Royal Yacht Squadron receiving a maximum entry of 50 for the series at Cowes on the Isle of Wight from July 4 to 10.

Ranked as the finest production yachts in the world, the Swans competing will range from the Swan 36 through to the Swan 68, with owners bringing their boats from Belgium, the Netherlands, France, Greece, the Dutch Antilles and Spain.
They will join British owners in a week of fine sailing and social activities that only Cowes can provide.
News Limited Australia chairman LACHLAN MURDOCH owns a Swan 55 in Sydney.
*Peter Campbell is editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
